problem: Learning-based navigation (end-to-end RL, learned mapping/localization/planning modules) was evaluated separately from classic modular robotics pipelines (SLAM + planning + control), with different environments and protocols. As a result there was no fair head-to-head comparison on realistic, previously unseen 3D indoor environments with continuous state and no ground-truth map or pose.
motivation: Learning methods promise to beat hand-engineered systems, but most learned navigation modules assume a discrete state space, a GT map or pose, or prior experience with the environment. Classic pipelines were usually run on custom robots or in small simulations. A common benchmark is needed to show the real strengths and weaknesses of each paradigm, how they depend on sensors (none / RGB / RGB-D), and how far both are from human performance.
key_idea: Implement a complete classic modular PointGoal pipeline (ORB-SLAM2 localization, depth-binning obstacle mapper, D* Lite planner, rule-based controller) and a strong end-to-end learned agent (DFP / Belief DFP) in the same MINOS environments, then compare them against a human under identical action spaces, sensor suites and metrics.
insight: With RGB-D input a properly tuned classic pipeline clearly beats the RL agent (mean SPL 67.9 vs 49.1), and the learned agent only marginally beats a 'blind' straight-to-goal classic baseline (mean SPL 45.9). The blind baseline should therefore replace random agents as the minimal PointGoal baseline. The classic system's weak point is localization: RGB-only ORB-SLAM collapses (mean SPL 6.1) because the pure rotations/forward motions and textureless surfaces make it re-initialize repeatedly, while the learned RGB agent degrades gracefully (44.0). Giving the classic agent GT pose adds 8-16 SPL points, and depth estimated from mono/stereo only partly recovers it (Table 4: e.g. 37.5-47.5 SPL on M3D vs 70.2 with GT depth). Clutter helps SLAM, so the classic agent does better in furnished/MP3D scenes than in empty ones. Humans (86.7-90.5 SPL) still beat even the classic agent given GT pose and map; the paper attributes this to imperfect MINOS maps and a controller that tracks paths poorly under severely discretized actions.
method: Localization: ORB-SLAM2 (RGB or RGB-D mode) outputs a 6-DOF pose. On tracking failure the map is reset (this worked better than re-localizing). For RGB-only, scale is fixed by a hard-coded look-down/look-up routine using the known agent height (~4 s of budget).

Mapping: a 2D obstacle grid with 10x10 cm cells. Depth points are reprojected to a top view, points above agent height or at ground level are dropped, points are binned, and a cell is occupied when its max point count exceeds a threshold (128 points for RGB-D). Without depth, the sparse ORB-SLAM point cloud is used with a lower threshold (30). Thresholds are tuned on the train set.

Planning: D* Lite shortest path on an 8-connected grid (diagonal edges weighted sqrt(2)). Unobserved cells are treated as traversable, and the plan is incrementally replanned as newly discovered obstacles change the map.

Locomotion: a PID-inspired rule controller for the discrete forward/turn-left/turn-right actions. It picks a waypoint d1=0.5 m ahead on the path, rotates if heading error > phi=15 deg and otherwise moves forward, switches waypoint when within d2=0.15 m, and takes a random action with p=0.1. 'Done' is triggered by a threshold on goal distance.

Learned agent (DFP): Direct Future Prediction predicts future measurements (goal distance, sin/cos of goal direction) for every action from stacked 4-frame grayscale/depth (128x128), action history and goal inputs, and picks the argmax of the objective. It is trained with supervised MSE via Adam (lr 1e-5, batch 32), 5M steps, epsilon-greedy from 0.95 down to 0.1, GroupNorm, and 4 parallel simulators.

Belief DFP (BDFP): an interpretable DFP variant that predicts, for each action and horizon, softmax-normalized egocentric belief maps of the agent's future position (16x16 per the supplement; the main text says 25x25). Future measurements are dot products with a measurement map of Euclidean distance to goal, and the action minimizing expected distance is chosen. It is trained with measurement MSE plus MSE on the belief maps against GT future positions.

Benchmark protocol: MINOS PointGoal on SunCG Empty, SunCG Furnished and Matterport3D; blind / RGB / RGB-D inputs plus oracle GT-pose and GT-pose+map variants; mono (fine-tuned Hu et al. ResNet-50) and stereo (OpenCV StereoSGBM+WLS) depth for the RGB classic agent; a human baseline with the same action space and 128x128 RGB; metrics SR, SPL and Pace.

setting.backbone: Two systems: (1) classic modular pipeline = ORB-SLAM2 + depth-binning grid mapper + D* Lite + rule-based controller (non-learned, a few thresholds tuned on the train split); (2) Belief DFP / DFP small CNN+MLP policy trained from scratch with GroupNorm
setting.training_data: MINOS train split environments (SunCG with texture randomization; Matterport3D) with random start-goal pairs, 5M environment steps (~5.8 days of real-time experience) per learned agent. Classic pipeline: only threshold/controller parameters tuned on the train set. For the mono-depth variant, a NYU-pretrained ResNet-50 (Hu et al.) is fine-tuned on data extracted from MINOS, separately for SunCG and Matterport3D.
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB and/or depth (depth range 0.001-4.0 m; 256x256 for classic, 128x128 grayscale 4-frame stack for learned) plus the goal vector relative to the agent (polar: distance and direction) at every step. 'Blind' variants get only the goal vector.
setting.action_space: Discrete: move forward / turn left / turn right (apply linear/angular force in MINOS; continuous state), plus a 'Done' action triggered by a goal-distance threshold. Time budget 50 s = 500 actions.
setting.simulator: MINOS (SunCG synthetic houses, furnished and empty; Matterport3D scans)
setting.privileged: Main setting: none beyond the PointGoal specification, i.e. the goal's relative distance and direction are provided at every time step (acts as a perfect goal-relative GPS). Oracle ablations additionally give the classic agent the MINOS GT pose, or GT pose plus the MINOS map.

numbers_note: The paper never explicitly names the split used for Tables 3-5/11-12. It says fixed start-goal sets are used 'for validation and test', so 'test' is assumed. Episodes are the paper's own filtered MINOS sets, not Habitat PointNav, so they are not directly comparable to Habitat MP3D-PointNav numbers. Learned RGB-D SR on Matterport3D is 46.9 in Table 11 but 47.0 in Table 5. Other own variants reported but not listed above: Classic RGB SPL 9.4/4.4/4.7; Learned RGB SPL 49.9/44.8/37.4; Learned blind SPL 52.9/13.8/27.7; Classic RGB-D + MINOS pose & map SPL 81.8/81.5/85.1 (SR 85.8/87.0/87.9); Classic RGB + MonoDepth SPL 43.8/47.3/37.5 and RGB + StereoDepth SPL 30.2/34.7/47.3 (Table 4, SunCG-E/SunCG-F/M3D). Table 2 compares SR on the MINOS Small/Medium task sets against Savva et al.: Ours-DFP 74.5/52.0 (Empty), 64.5/46.7 (Furnished), 41.0* (M3D Medium); Ours-BDFP 78.1/55.0, 60.0/47.9, 41.0*. The M3D evaluation set there differs from Savva et al. Human: SPL 90.5/87.9/86.7 and SR 97.0/100.0/95.3 over 68/68/43 trials. Per-path-length curves appear only in Figures 5 and 9.
results: With RGB-D input the classic modular pipeline reaches SPL 65.7 / 67.7 / 70.2 on SunCG Empty / Furnished / Matterport3D (mean 67.9). This beats the Belief-DFP learned agent (54.6 / 47.2 / 45.5, mean 49.1), which is itself only slightly better than a blind straight-to-goal classic baseline (mean 45.9). Classic with RGB only collapses (mean SPL 6.1) while learned RGB holds up (44.0), and depth estimated from mono/stereo recovers the classic agent only partially. GT pose raises classic SPL to 78.8-84.5. A human using 128x128 RGB (SPL 86.7-90.5) beats every agent, including classic with GT pose and map.
limitations: Only the simple PointGoal task, with the relative goal vector provided at every step. Evaluation sets are small (100 episodes on Matterport3D, 340 per SunCG variant) and filtered, in the MINOS simulator with a severely discretized force-based action space.

Only one representative classic pipeline and one learned family (DFP/BDFP) are tested. The RL agent is trained for only 5M steps and has no explicit memory structure, so its weakness may reflect sample inefficiency rather than a limit of learning.
The human baseline is a single subject who may remember layouts across trials, and MINOS GT maps are imperfect (missing doors), which complicates the oracle comparisons.
